source_of_truth: Curated static reference: iOS Spin & Dine v2.x flows as documented in this fixture. NOT a live read from any external repo — the fixture is reproducible from this file alone. Treated as a generic parity-goal example per D013; project name is content, not a product-code dependency.

user_journeys.name: onboarding
user_journeys.description: First-launch flow: user lands on splash, accepts terms, is prompted for location permission (with skip option), then sees an empty home screen with a 'Get started' CTA. Tapping CTA opens the radius-picker sheet. After radius is set, the home screen populates with 'Spin' button + nearby restaurants list. iOS supports a returning-user path that bypasses radius-picker if a saved radius exists in user defaults.
acceptance_signals: Splash → terms → location prompt sequence renders identically on both platforms
Location-skipped state shows the same 'Set radius manually' empty CTA
Returning-user fast path: app opens directly to home_populated when saved radius exists
Radius-picker sheet uses the same 1mi / 5mi / 10mi / custom presets

user_journeys.name: restaurant-voting
user_journeys.description: Core 'spin' interaction: user taps Spin, wheel animates and lands on a restaurant card. Card shows name, cuisine, distance, hours, price tier, and a star rating. User can tap thumbs-up (saves to favorites + records vote), thumbs-down (records negative vote, never re-shows for 7 days), or 'spin again'. iOS supports a 'no-network cached fallback': when offline, the wheel pulls from the last-cached restaurant pool with a 'cached results' badge. iOS also supports a 'no-results-after-relaxation' state: if every nearby restaurant is voted-down within the past week, a coaching message offers to clear vote history or expand radius.
acceptance_signals: Spin animation duration matches across platforms (~1.2s)
Vote actions persist across app restarts
7-day cooldown on thumbs-down honored on both platforms
Offline cached fallback shows 'cached results' badge and continues to spin from local pool
no_results_after_relaxation state triggers the same coaching prompt copy and CTAs

user_journeys.name: saved-lists
user_journeys.description: Users can organize favorited restaurants into named lists ('Date night', 'Quick lunch', etc.). Saved-lists tab shows all lists with cover thumbnails (4 most-recent restaurants per list). Tapping a list opens detail view with restaurants ordered by date-saved. Long-press on a list offers rename / reorder / share. iOS has a 'shared list' state: a list owned by another user (received via share link) shows a banner 'Shared by <name>' and read-only mode for non-owners.
acceptance_signals: Lists tab renders 4-tile cover thumbnail consistently
Long-press menu items match across platforms
Shared-list read-only state visually distinct from owner state
Rename modal accepts up to 32 chars with the same validation

user_journeys.name: subscription-ux
user_journeys.description: Free tier supports 5 spins/day. Pro tier ($4.99/mo, $39/yr) supports unlimited spins + voice 'spin' shortcut + family sharing. Subscription is purchased via in-app StoreKit (iOS) / Play Billing (Android). Subscription state surfaces in the profile tab as a tile showing tier + renewal date + manage link. iOS has a 'grace period' state: if renewal fails, the user retains Pro features for 16 days while StoreKit retries.
acceptance_signals: Daily spin counter resets at local midnight on both platforms
Pro upsell appears at the same trigger points
Grace period gives identical 16-day buffer on both platforms
Purchase failure surfaces a recoverable error with a Retry CTA

required_evidence: Side-by-side screenshot comparison: iOS vs Android for each user journey's primary states
State coverage matrix: for each journey, for each state, mark iOS✓/Android✓/missing
Network-failure walk: spin while offline; verify cached fallback + uncached error states
Subscription edge cases: forced renewal failure to trigger grace period; verify 16-day buffer
Saved-lists shared-mode walk: receive a shared list via deep link, confirm read-only banner
non_goals: Web platform parity (web is not a target surface for v2)
Tablet-specific layouts (phone-first; tablet handled via stretched-phone for v2)
completion_test: Android matches iOS for the four user journeys end-to-end including state coverage, wiring (deep links + share extensions), and edge cases (offline fallback, subscription grace period, shared-list read-only). A user who switched between an iOS and Android device mid-flow should see identical behavior at every state transition.
